title: Maranao (MGySgt to Pvt) EMOS (2629, 2641, 2691), DIR INTEL
raw_text:
32.     MOS 2748, Maranao (MGySgt to Pvt) EMOS (2629, 2641, 2691), DIR INTEL

    a. Summary. Linguist MOSs are EMOSs used in conjunction with the 2629,
2641 and 2691 Primary MOSs or Necessary MOS 2642 that indicate specialized
foreign language skills. Linguists supervise and participate in language
translation/interpretation activities pertaining primarily to military
operational and intelligence activities. The linguist MOSs will be assigned
as EMOSs to identify those Marines with qualifying foreign language skills.
The titles and MOSs will be used to identify billets in T/Os requiring
specific foreign language skills as required by the billet MOS (BMOS) or
additional skills designator (ASD). This EMOS will be assigned and voided by
the Director of Intelligence only.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must be proficient in Maranao.


                                         3-205                      Enclosure (1)
 3123                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L



       c.   Requirements

        (1) Qualifying DLPT scores alone are not justification for EMOS
assignment. Marines must successfully complete the required course of
instruction at the Defense Language Institute, Language Training Detachment,
or designated government-funded language course and achieve minimum ILR
proficiency as required by the appropriate PMOS or NMOS in two modalities of
listening, reading or speaking portions of the Defense Language Proficiency
Test (DLPT). (Note: By exception, individuals may qualify for this EMOS
when language training is not required, but Marine meets proficiency
requirements and language fulfills PMOS, NMOS or billet requirements. In
these instances, requests for EMOS assignment must be submitted to Director
of Intelligence for eligibility determination).

        (2) Maintain minimum ILR level proficiency with as required by the
appropriate PMOS or NMOS in two modalities of listening, reading, or speaking
portions of the DLPT.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Conducts bi-directional consecutive interpretation of target
language to English and English to target language using phraseology selected
to preserve the original intent, meaning, and emphasis.

        (2) Phrases ideas to avoid language that is stilted, unnatural, and
difficult to understand.

        (3) Displays an impartial attitude toward each speaker and to facts
and opinions expressed.

        (4) Interprets into either English or target language the statements
made by participants in conferences, working parties, and all similar
activities.

        (5) Interviews friendly non-English speaking civilians such as
police, clergymen, and other citizens to obtain information of military
value.

        (6) Writes reports, including opinion as to the credibility of the
person interviewed, for use by unit commander and for dissemination to lower,
adjacent, and higher headquarters.

        (7) Translates into either English or the target language, written
material of both a technical and nontechnical nature.

        (8) Establishes a file of language reference materials, English and
foreign language dictionaries, and glossaries of military terms.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Interpreters and Translators 27-3091.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
